decision_reason: The assigned source is a public Apache-licensed Android operator client for the notable, publicly funded Vxnaid vaccination platform. Hold because the product architecture also depends on separately sourced OpenMRS/API/backend and commercially licensed iris-biometric components, while the Apache grant in this repository does not establish an eligible grant for those material product components; I also found no primary evidence tying the 2025 Uganda adaptation to this exact source snapshot.

government_provenance.note: The IHI/IMI EBODAC factsheet says Vxnaid was established as a result of EBODAC and later used in COVID-19 campaigns; the same project record identifies EU funding of €20,328,856 (grant 115847) alongside EFPIA co-funding. This is product-specific public-private EU-funded provenance, not a claim of sovereign-state authorship.

public_source.note: The assigned public repository contains the Android application source, build files, and project documentation without credentials; its readme identifies it as the operator tablet application.

eligible_license.note: The repository root carries Apache-2.0 for the first-party Android client. The project readme requires an OpenMRS backend and iris module and links separate software terms; the architecture also lists an intermediate API and Neurotechnology biometric system, whose source grants are not covered by this Android repository. The readme and iris setup docs expressly require Neurotechnology licenses. Product-wide eligible-license scope is therefore unresolved.

primary_evidence.note: Primary project reporting and the IHI factsheet document real vaccination-campaign use, while this 2025 Uganda conference poster reports a Vxnaid immunization deployment. The poster does not identify the assigned source tree or establish that this repository version is the distributed client; source-to-current-deployment parity remains unresolved.

product_identity: Vxnaid operator Android tablet client, a component of the wider vaccine-administration platform for participant identification, dose eligibility, and visit logging
agency: European Union / Innovative Medicines Initiative 2 Joint Undertaking (public co-funder of EBODAC, grant 115847); Johnson & Johnson Global Public Health and partners developed Vxnaid
geography: International public-private project; designed for African vaccination campaigns, with reported DRC and Uganda use
license: Apache-2.0 for first-party Android client code in this repository only; platform-wide grant unresolved because backend/API and licensed biometric components are separate
family_note: The older Johnson & Johnson Vxnaid wiki describes four distinct components (Android tablet app, OpenMRS backend, intermediate API, and Neurotechnology iris system); separate archived J&J OpenMRS distribution/module repositories exist. Do not treat this client repository's Apache grant as licensing the entire platform.
status_note: Root LICENSE first appears in a 2022-06-24 commit; assigned repository's latest commit observed is 2024-06-05. The IHI factsheet supports historic and COVID-campaign product use, but the exact 2025 deployment/source correspondence and current distributable license boundary are not demonstrated. The readme links separate Software Terms of Use that were not independently accessible during this review.

decision_reason: The Council of Lombardy identifies and owns this exact legislative-act management product, the public repository provides its source and AGPL-3.0-only grant, and the Council's current GEA statistics plus 2025 proceedings establish product-specific operational use. The quiet repository has a documented current-use/support signal.

government_provenance.note: The official Developers Italia software record names GeA 1.3, identifies the Consiglio regionale della Lombardia as publisher and manager, links this source repository, and describes the Council's legislative and administrative act workflow.

public_source.note: The public canonical repository contains the application modules, source, project description, and installation/deployment material without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The root LICENSE contains the full GNU AGPL version 3 text and the publiccode.yml declares AGPL-3.0-only for the software. The repository documents separate licenses for documentation/assets and third-party components; this grant is scoped to first-party software, not every bundled item.

primary_evidence.note: The Council's page updated 19 March 2026 publishes 2024–2025 usage statistics for the named GEA 'Elenco generale Atti' database and describes its legislative/administrative records. Official 2025 Council proceedings also direct staff to retrieve documents in GEA, corroborating recent operational use.

product_identity: GeA (Sistema Informativo Gestione Atti), the Council of Lombardy's legislative and administrative act workflow/document-management system
license: AGPL-3.0-only for first-party software code; documentation/assets and third-party components have separately stated licenses
family_note: GeA is the Council's legislative-act workflow product and named Elenco generale Atti database, not the separate GeDASI system for acts of political direction and oversight.
status_note: The root license/source commit is dated 2020-08-04; latest source commit observed is 2023-12-11. The Council's 2024–2025 GEA usage statistics are posted on an official page verified/updated in March 2026, and official 2025 proceedings reference GEA in active committee workflow. The software record and repository describe stable government software; quiet development is offset by this exact, current-use evidence.

decision_reason: The Council of Lombardy identifies this exact attendance and councillor-management system as its software, has a 2024 contract for its maintenance and evolution, and the current public repository contains the source with an explicit AGPL-3.0 grant. The first licensed source year and current operational support are documented.

government_provenance.note: The Council's 26 July 2024 award names GE.CO. as open-source software of the Consiglio regionale della Lombardia and funds ordinary maintenance, technical support, and evolutionary development for twelve months, with a possible four-month extension.

public_source.note: The public repository contains the C#/.NET application, database scripts, project documentation, and usage screenshots without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The root LICENSE is the complete GNU AGPL version 3 text, and the current README explicitly grants AGPL 3.0 to first-party code/database while assigning documentation CC BY 4.0 and identifying separate third-party library licenses and a proprietary Council logo. publiccode.yml still says GPL-2.0-or-later; that stale metadata conflicts with the full root grant and current README, so the review scopes the proven grant to code/database and records the metadata discrepancy rather than treating it as the governing source license.

primary_evidence.note: The Council's 2024 procurement is specifically for maintenance and evolutionary development of GE.CO.; an official Council process-risk sheet describes how GE.CO. supplies monthly councillor attendance data used for absence deductions and required transparency reporting.

product_identity: Gestione Consiglieri (GeCo), the Council of Lombardy application for councillor/assessor institutional profiles, assembly-body attendance and absence workflows, and related transparency reporting
license: AGPL-3.0-only for first-party code and database; documentation is CC BY 4.0, third-party libraries have separate licenses, and Council logo is proprietary. publiccode.yml has a conflicting GPL-2.0-or-later label.
family_note: This is the Council's GeCo councillor profile/attendance system, distinct from GEA legislative-act management and GeDASI parliamentary act handling.
status_note: The first root LICENSE and functional source commit is 2020-11-05; repository head observed 2026-09-15. The 2024 service award is for twelve months with extension option, and the Council's process document explains production attendance-data handling. The README's 2026 edits and recent source commits support current maintenance; publiccode.yml's GPL-2.0-or-later field is inconsistent with the attached full AGPL v3 license and current README grant.

decision_reason: The Council's report establishes its PEM platform, which the current repository identifies as the PEM module of the evolved GeDASI portal. The source is public under AGPL-3.0-only, is recently maintained, and the Council provides a live portal and current usage statistics for the integrated service.

government_provenance.note: The Council's 2021 report says it decided to create the PEM multiuser platform for remote preparation, signature, and filing of amendments and subamendments; Council procurement records later name the same system as PEM-DASI/GeDASI for evolutive development and maintenance.

public_source.note: The public canonical repository now describes the integrated GeDASI source and explicitly documents its PEM and DASI modules, source layout, installation/user documentation, and current platform identity.

eligible_license.note: The root file is the full GNU AGPL version 3 text and the project README declares AGPL-3.0 for first-party repository code; third-party libraries are separately listed and the Council logo is explicitly proprietary, so neither is represented as part of the AGPL grant.

primary_evidence.note: The Council publishes 2024–2025 access/search/page statistics for the current GEDASI acts database and marked the page verified/updated in July 2026; the live GeDASI login and 2023 evolutive-maintenance notice corroborate current service distribution and use.

product_identity: GeDASI (PEM-DASI), the Council of Lombardy's integrated digital acts portal; the assigned PEM repository is the maintained source for the amendment-presentation module within the wider portal
license: AGPL-3.0-only for first-party software code in the repository; third-party libraries and Council logo are separately licensed/unlicensed
family_note: The repository is no longer a stand-alone PEM application: its current README says it is the shared GeDASI platform, with PEM and DASI modules and a single portal. Identify it as GeDASI (PEM-DASI), not as a duplicate independent DASI product.
status_note: The first commit with LICENSE.md and substantial source is 2021-04-11; repository head observed 2026-09-24. The README says the Council expanded PEM into DASI and renamed the integrated platform GeDASI after its third development phase. The official service page reports GEDASI use in 2024–2025 and was updated in 2026.

decision_reason: CNR's agreement with Italy's Digital Agency explicitly states that Selezioni On Line was developed at CNR, links this exact repository, and documents CNR SaaS operation and AgID adoption. The current public service, source, user documentation, and exact AGPL grant-bearing history meet all four checks.

government_provenance.note: The signed CNR–AgID collaboration agreement says Selezioni On Line was developed at CNR, identifies this exact Developers Italia entry/repository, and describes AgID's adoption of the software for its own recruitment processes; it distinguishes CNR as developer/host and AgID as public-sector user.

public_source.note: The canonical public repository contains the recruitment application, source and Docker deployment instructions, and user/technical documentation without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The first-party publiccode.yml declares AGPL-3.0-or-later; the root LICENSE contains the complete GNU AGPL version 3 text and the README applies that license to Cool-Jconon. This grant is scoped to CNR-authored project code; listed dependencies and integrated Alfresco/OpenMRS components retain their own licenses.

primary_evidence.note: The CNR–AgID agreement documents the software as a hosted CNR service for public recruitment, technical/functional documentation at the exact source listing, and AgID use; the live CNR Selezioni On Line portal and CNR recruitment page remain active.

product_identity: CNR E-Recruitment / Selezioni On Line (Cool-Jconon), software for public recruitment procedures from call publication and applications through commission scoring and ranking publication
agency: Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche (CNR); Agenzia per l'Italia Digitale (AgID) is a documented adopting public agency
license: AGPL-3.0-or-later for first-party Cool-Jconon code; dependencies and integrated platforms have separate licenses
family_note: Cool-Jconon is CNR's e-recruitment product built on/integrated with Cool/Alfresco; the project grant does not relicense those separately identified platform dependencies.
status_note: The first repository LICENSE grant commit is 2019-06-28; current source commit observed 2026-09-23. The CNR–AgID agreement states CNR hosts it as SaaS and offers public administrations reuse or SaaS, while current CNR listings and the live portal establish ongoing service distribution. The source's releaseDate field is 2026 metadata and was not used as the source year.
